SUAS-014 — SuperUnicode Vertical Text Layout

The runtime counterpart of UAX #50: one 8-byte orientation record, a total answer for every codepoint, and a lookup that is a hash and a bounded probe.

SUAS-014 (SUVTL) is the fourteenth SuperUnicode Architecture Standard and the runtime counterpart of UAX #50, the Vertical Text Layout annex. UAX #50 defines the Vertical_Orientation (vo) property in prose and ships it as VerticalOrientation.txt — semicolon-delimited ranges tagged U, R, Tu or Tr, with narrative glyph-change notes every implementation reads at run time. SUVTL keeps the property and closes the architecture around it: a byte-packed table, a bounded lookup, and a verification surface the compiler must satisfy before it emits a record.

SUVTL does not re-implement SUAS-006 (STS). STS decides where a grapheme cluster begins and ends; SUVTL takes the first character of a cluster as the cluster’s orientation, with the enclosing-mark exception of UAX #50. The two compose; neither re-derives the other.

Why a binary property

Aspect UAX #50 SUVTL
Definition A text data file, parsed at run time A static binary table, compiled at build time
Orientation A four-letter tag on a range line Three value bits; the tag is a derived view
Glyph changes Narrative tables A single TRANSFORM flag; the prose stays in the reference layer
Lookup Search the file A hash and a bounded probe — O(1) expected
Unlisted codepoint Undefined A total algorithmic default — every codepoint answers
Failure mode An implementer’s own reconciliation The verifier names the first of eleven defects

The orientation record

Four fields, 8 bytes, no padding on any supported ABI. They are the seeding sketch’s fields, verbatim: codepoint, orientation_flags, baseline_offset and reserved.

typedef struct {
uint32_t codepoint; /* Base SUCS codepoint */
uint16_t orientation_flags; /* SUVTL_ORIENT_* + SUVTL_FLAG_* */
uint8_t baseline_offset; /* signed 1/16-em vertical adjustment */
uint8_t reserved; /* must be zero */
} suvtl_glyph_layout_t;

The four values, read off the bits

UAX #50’s four values are encoded by the three bits the seeding sketch exposed, rather than a separate enum: UPRIGHT, ROTATED and TRANSFORM. There is no second, redundant value field to keep in sync, and a caller that only wants “does this rotate?” tests one bit.

Value Encoding Meaning Fallback
U 0x0001 = UPRIGHT Upright —
R 0x0002 = ROTATED Rotated 90° clockwise —
Tu 0x0005 = UPRIGHT | TRANSFORM Transformed upright U
Tr 0x0006 = ROTATED | TRANSFORM Transformed rotated R

Three orthogonal flags sit above the value: CUSTOM_FLOW (a Native/neography vertical-flow declaration), SQUARED (a squared katakana or ideographic word) and QUOTATION (a font-substituted quotation mark). baseline_offset is a signed 1/16-em vertical adjustment, zero by default.

The grapheme-cluster rule

UAX #50 defines a cluster’s orientation as its first character’s, unless the cluster contains an enclosing combining mark (general category Me), in which case the whole cluster is U. suas_suvtl_cluster_orientation applies that rule to one cluster the caller supplies; suas_suvtl_is_enclosing_mark answers the Me question from a small curated set of Me ranges, so a caller need not have loaded SUCD. The engine never computes cluster boundaries — that is STS.

Zones and the total default

A layout query may name only the Bridge plane, the RNUR neography carve-out, or the custom-conscript Native plane. A codepoint with no curated record is not unknown: suas_suvtl_get_layout_properties synthesizes an algorithmic default from the codepoint’s vertical-behaviour group — CJK and the remainder upright, Latin/Greek/Cyrillic rotated — and returns true. It returns false only for an inadmissible zone or a NULL output. The property is total.

Zone Range Text space?
BRIDGE 0x00000000–0x0010FFFF Yes
SCP 0x00110000–0x0011FFFF No — Control Plane
NATIVE rest of 0x00120000–0x7FFFFFEF Yes — custom conscript space
RNUR 0x00160000–0x0016FFFF Yes — neography
TRAP / SENTINEL / EXTSUCS terminals and plugin space No

The curated roster

The compiled table carries the full UAX #50 Table 3 Tu/Tr roster — the characters whose default glyph is not acceptable in vertical text and for which a font must supply a separate vertical form — plus the Native/neography custom-flow declarations. It is a curated subset of the SUCD reference layer; extending it is a data update, never an API change.

Block Value Flag
Quotation marks Tr QUOTATION
Brackets, punctuation, small kana, Bopomofo, fullwidth forms Tr —
Squared katakana / ideographic words Tu SQUARED
Native / RNUR declarations U CUSTOM_FLOW

Lookup and its cost

Operation Cost
suas_suvtl_init_engine O(n) once, n ≤ 512, no allocation
suas_suvtl_get_layout_properties O(1) expected — one hash and a bounded probe
suas_suvtl_orientation_of / _is_upright / _is_rotated / _is_transformed O(1)
suas_suvtl_cluster_orientation O(cluster) — the enclosing-mark scan plus one lookup
suas_suvtl_validate_table O(n²) worst case — a compiler-time verifier

Verification names the defect

suas_suvtl_validate_table returns the first of eleven named outcomes: a NULL table, a count over capacity, an unordered pair, a duplicate codepoint, a codepoint past the space, an inadmissible codepoint, a value that names no orientation, a reserved or contradictory flag bit, a nonzero reserved byte, or a custom-flow claim outside the RNUR set. An empty registry is valid: an implementation with no curated records ships zero rows and conforms.

Classification note

SUVTL is a SUAS core invariant, registered as SUAS-014, the number immediately after SUAS-013 (SISR). One element of the SUTS framing survives deliberately: the registry contents are optional version data, so an implementation with no curated records ships an empty table and remains conformant — while the engine, the record layout, the lookup contract and the verification rules are mandatory architecture.

The seeding sketch named its offline layer “SUCA”. In this corpus SUCA is already the SuperUnicode Collation Algorithm (SUTS-001), so SUVTL names SUCD (SUAS-012) as its reference layer — exactly as SIP, SCSS and SISR already do.

Reference implementation: include/suas/suas_suvtl.h + src/suas/suas_suvtl.c (freestanding C99, no heap), registered in suas_static and in the SSRE registry as a MANDATORY specification.

Source of truth: docs/suas/SUAS-014-suvtl.md in the repository.
